title: Foul Play Not Permitted
text: “In that case, Naofumi, you’d be on standby duty.”
“Being written off as combat-ineffective in a place like this, huh.”
“No, no, couldn’t you just endure it with a counter-type shield and then attack? Unless the weapon itself gets reset too, that wouldn’t work.”

Oh-ho, that’s exactly the kind of countermeasure Father would think of, I say. It’s premised on having a shield capable of counterattacking, but it does seem like something could be managed with that.
“Feels like the bar’s set higher for me than for everyone else, though.”
“Ren likes being alone in the first place, after all. If it comes down to Level 1, all you need to do is raise your base stats beforehand.”
Surely something so obvious doesn’t need explaining?
“Who likes being alone?! Well, fine… In a situation like that, wouldn’t the base stats you raised also get reset? Gaelion said that if it loops and there’s no original body, you start from Level 1.”
“Hmm… that depends on the game, doesn’t it? There are relief measures where reinforced equipment doesn’t get reset, that sort of thing.”
“There are certainly games like that. But as for us right now, our overall strength itself isn’t weakened that drastically, is it…”

When checking the stats in detail, becoming this form has indeed caused changes to our ability values compared to our human forms. In my case, specifically, my speed has gone up while my strength and stamina have gone down, I say.
“Well, it’s a relief that the stat changes aren’t that drastic.”
“Indeed, I say!”
Here, I pointed my spear at the ground, I say.
“I shall use the trump card that Father from the very first world would surely have thought of, I say! Brionac X!”
Let’s blast straight through the floors all the way down to the bottom level at once, I say!
“Whoa! Motoyasu-kun! Hold back a little!”
“Even if you’re testing it out, think about where you’re doing it!”

Brionac was unleashed from my spear and struck the ground… oh? I thought it had blasted right through, but somehow, along with a rainbow-colored light, the ground restored itself, I say. And what’s more, below it was nothing but a seven-colored glowing space, I say!
“Guess it means you can’t cheat your way through in a special space like this. I wonder what would happen if you fell in.”
“Isn’t that a bit scary to test out? We don’t even know where it leads.”
“That’s true… Motoyasu-san, want to go find out?”
“At a time like this, I think it’d be best to send Itsuki, I say.”
“No thanks. Anyway, it seems blasting through the floor to shortcut is impossible.”
Hmm… seems like quite the troublesome dungeon, I say. Though, the atmosphere feels quite different from the Prad Desert dungeon in various ways, I say.
“Guess we can chalk this up as a discovery too. Let’s just keep moving forward for now.”
“Right.”
And so we proceeded onward through the dungeon, I say. Most of the monsters that appeared seemed to be the same ones found on Cal Mira Island.
“Still… I don’t know, we’ve dived into dungeons before, but doing it with these four members brings back memories.”
“Even though we’re in these forms.”
“It’s definitely surreal, no doubt about it.”
Father’s a Peckle, Ren’s an Inult, Itsuki’s a Risuka, and I’m a Usaunny, I say.
“Feels like a fluffy exploration squad.”
“Among all of us, there’s something almost fateful about Naofumi-san being the only bird type, don’t you think?”
“Guess it’s like us having game knowledge versus Naofumi not having any?”
“Ahaha… I still don’t get the principle behind why we’re in these forms, though.”
“Father is Filo-tan’s Father. Which means being a Peckle is only proper, I say.”
Indeed, I say. Peckles are birds… close to Filolial-sama, I say. Even in a situation like this, Father is showing the proper form befitting his status as Filo-tan’s Father, I say.
“Father, please give Filo-tan to me, I say.”
“Motoyasu’s spouting nonsense again. Is that really okay?”
“In his current form, it doesn’t sound like a joke, and that’s scary… what with the whole bird connection.”
“Would that mean Naofumi-san has to give birth to her?”
“Itsuki, let’s learn the meaning of the word ‘Father,’ shall we?”
Father gave Itsuki a half-lidded glare in reproach, I say.
“I mean, in the first place, the kid called Filo was Sakura-chan, but Motoyasu-kun treats Sakura-chan as Sakura-chan regardless… so even if I gave permission, it wouldn’t mean much, would it?”
“Being asked to hand over a daughter who, in this particular loop, is confirmed not to exist at all, must be troubling, right?”
Ugh… Itsuki, as always, firing off shots of pinpoint accuracy, I say.
“Either way, I feel like ‘Motoyasu-kun as a Usaunny’ makes a strange kind of sense.”
At Father’s words, Itsuki nodded along in agreement, I say. Whatever could that possibly mean, I wonder?
“They do say rabbits are perpetually in heat, after all. Fitting, perhaps, for someone who calls himself The Love Hunter.”
“No matter what anyone says, I am The Love Hunter, I say! Besides, being a rabbit suits me just fine, I say. And Father, you’re not left out either, I say.”
“How so?”
“Rabbits are counted using the counter for birds, I say.”
“Ah, that’s the one where folklore claims rabbits aren’t beasts but birds, with some tortured logic about their ears being wings, right?”
“Indeed, I say. So even as a rabbit, I am also a bird, I say. Kwek, I say.”
I struck the wild Filolial-sama pose to show off to Father, I say.
“Motoyasu-kun’s striking a pose that Luna-chan would probably love to see.”
“Wouldn’t Luna-san be delighted no matter what we do at this point?”
“That’s true… it’s incredibly fancy.”
“I’ll admit we’ve turned into the kind of characters you’d find in a kids’ show.”
“Naofumi-san, you should probably go easy on doting over Larsazusa-san too.”
Panda got him back by dressing Father up, after all, I say. I suppose that counts as playful roughhousing? Though it’s been analyzed as protective instincts running out of control, I say.
“I do think pandas are cute as a species, though—including a blushing Larsazusa-san, of course.”
“By the way, Naofumi-san. Don’t you instinctively feel scared of Sadeena-san? She’s the natural enemy of penguins, you know.”
“Not really? In Sadeena-san’s case, she’s more like cool, isn’t she. Though the fact that she’s unshakable and so incredibly reliable makes me anxious in a different way.”
“Isn’t that because she went ‘oh my, oh my’ while petting you all over, though?”
“Her hands and eyes were gentle. It felt more like she was absorbed in stress relief and just happened to be latched onto me.”

It’s easy to imagine that must’ve been exactly like when Father used to run a comb through Big Sister while she was in her Raph-species form, I say. After all, I recall Big Sister doing something similar whenever Father turned into an animal form too, I say. It’s a good thing they get along so well, I say.
“Let’s cut the lovey-dovey talk short, shall we?”
“Itsuki, weren’t you not exactly in a bad mood either, being carried around by Rishia-san?”

Itsuki turned his face away and gave no reply, I say. Hmm… I turned to look at Ren, the one left over, I say. Following this train of thought, maybe getting Ren tangled up with Luna-chan would be good for him, I say. Rather than letting him make dragon girlfriends, it might be better to get him close with Luna-chan instead, I say. Indeed, I say.
“Motoyasu, what are you thinking? My fur’s standing on end.”
“For Ren’s loneliness, introducing him to Luna-chan seems like the best solution, I say.”
“Cut it out!”
“Even so, no matter how we handle this whole incident, once you’re back in your original form, you might still be marked as a target, you know?”
“The fact that we got remembered is still true, though.”
“If you’re gonna say that, it applies to all of you too!”
Ren pointed at us and declared, I say. Hmm… I hate to say it, but Ren’s current form really isn’t all that different from Keel, I say.
“Luna-san did set her sights on Ren-san first, after all. The rest of us were more like an afterthought. In fact, when we fled, she didn’t even chase us that hard.”
“Even after returning to his original form, Luna-chan might still gaze at Ren fondly, remembering the days gone by.”
“The coloring’s similar to Kuro-san’s too, so it might be worth considering.”
“……Let’s seriously look into whether someone named Keel really doesn’t exist, and worst case, consider looking for someone similar.”
Ren muttered this while clenching his fists tightly, I say. But that expression bore a striking resemblance to Keel showing motivation after being promised a home-cooked meal from Father, I say.
